subject.title: [Bug]: TLS certificate pin mismatch loop when connecting through Cloudflare Tunnel/Access (anycast edge certs)

question: Should iOS Remote Domain mode identify the gateway by its hostname and system-trusted certificate chain, while direct/discovered gateway modes continue using an explicitly approved certificate fingerprint?
rationale: The current single-leaf identity cannot represent Cloudflare anycast, but globally disabling pinning would undo intentional security hardening and alter how trusted transport protects credential recovery.

options.title: Separate trust by connection mode
options.body: Use system CA and hostname validation for Remote Domain, retain explicit fingerprint pinning for direct/discovered or self-signed gateways, and migrate stored Remote Domain trust state.

options.title: Add a trust-mode selector
options.body: Keep fingerprint pinning as the default and let users explicitly choose system Web-PKI trust for reverse-proxy or anycast domains, at the cost of additional setup surface.

options.title: Keep leaf pinning only
options.body: Document Cloudflare anycast and similar rotating-edge services as unsupported, preserving the current security boundary but leaving this remote-use path blocked.

recommendation.title: Separate trust by connection mode
recommendation.body: Use system CA and hostname validation for Remote Domain, retain explicit fingerprint pinning for direct/discovered or self-signed gateways, and migrate stored Remote Domain trust state.

likelyOwner.reason: The most directly relevant merged history is the existing iOS rotated-certificate recovery implementation, with mbelinky and steipete providing broader iOS and security-boundary context.
